title: Fáj a Fejem – Saying What Hurts

sections.title: The body part is the subject
sections.content: To say something hurts, Hungarian puts the body part itself in the subject position, with a possessive suffix showing whose it is, and uses the verb fáj ("to hurt"). Fáj a fejem is literally "hurts my head" — there's no separate word for "I" or "my" the way English needs one; the -em ending on fejem already carries that meaning.

You can add a dative pronoun like nekem ("to me") for emphasis or clarity — Nekem fáj a fejem — but it's optional and usually dropped, exactly like with tetszik or ízlik. Without context, plain Fáj a fejem is understood as "my head".
